summary: Late-February 2026 polls show CDU ahead or near Greens, but the edge is narrow and uncertain under BW's 154-seat system.

Multi-party fragmentation (AfD, FDP, SPD, Linke) and turnout dynamics subtly reduce CDU's probability of the most seats.
Under the Zweitstimme-based system with a larger chamber, small swings can flip who has the most seats, supporting a lower posterior.

question: Will CDU win the most seats in the Baden-Württemberg Landtag election?
summary: Late-Feb 2026 polls place CDU ahead of Greens in Baden-Württemberg, lifting the probability of CDU being the largest party above the ensemble 29%.
Greens have been the largest party in two of the last three elections, which keeps Greens competitive and counteracts a CDU lead.
The new 154-seat Zweitstimme-based system adds uncertainty in translating votes to seats, offering both potential amplification and dampening of a CDU advantage.
Overall, a CDU win of the most seats is plausible but not assured; the estimate is calibrated around a mid-40% probability with substantial uncertainty near the decision date.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections about Greens’ historical dominance and late-swing risk are valid and important; polls suggesting CDU lead and seat projections under the new system justify raising the probability from the ensemble.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted upward from 0.29 to 0.43 to reflect credible late-Feb polling signals and seat projections showing CDU ahead or narrowly ahead; no implausible threshold arguments were used to justify downward bias.

forecasts.reference-class: Historical Baden-Württemberg Landtag elections since 2011, evaluating which party won the most seats: CDU in 2011; Greens in 2016 and 2021.

sources.claim: 2011: CDU was the largest party with 39.0% (60 seats); Greens 24.2% (36 seats).
2016: Greens with 30.3% (47 seats) surpassed CDU (27.0%) to become the strongest party.
Endgültiges 2016 Ergebnis: Greens 30.3% (47 seats); CDU 27.0% (42 seats).
2016: Greens 30.3% (47 seats); CDU 27% (42 seats); Greens largest.
2021: Greens 32.6% (58 seats); CDU 24.1% (42 seats).
Official 2021 results: Greens 32.6% (58 seats); CDU 24.1% (42 seats).
January 2026 polling: CDU ~29%; Greens ~23%; AfD ~20%; SPD ~8%; Left ~7%; FDP ~5%.
October 2025 poll: CDU ~29%; Greens ~20%; AfD ~21%.
May 2025 article: CDU leads; Greens second in the Baden-Württemberg poll landscape.
February 2026 Insa poll: CDU ~28%; Greens ~22% (momentary lead for CDU).
Infratest dimap (ARD) poll dated 25-02-2026: CDU 28%, Greens 27%, AfD 18%, SPD 7%, FDP 6%, Linke 5.5%, with parliamentary projection: CDU 37 seats vs Greens 35 seats.
Forschungsgruppe Wahlen poll dated 26-02-2026: CDU 27%, Greens 25%, AfD 19%, SPD 9%, FDP 6%, Linke 6%; projection: CDU 35 seats vs Greens 32 seats.
WELT reporting on ARD polling: CDU around 28%, Greens around 27% near election; seat distribution near 37 for CDU and 35 for Greens under the projection.
INSA survey cited: CDU 31% vs Greens 17%；Infras. dimap surveys also show CDU ahead (29% vs 20%).
January 22, 2026 poll shows CDU 29%, Greens 23%, AfD 20%, SPD 8%, Linke 7%, FDP 5%.

Overview of BW 2026 election with multiple poll snapshots; includes Infratest dimap and FGW-based figures illustrating CDU leading or closing gap with Greens and the effect of the new electoral system.
BWTrend poll (Infratest dimap for SWR/StZ) five months before the election shows CDU leading at about 29%, with AfD around 20% and Greens around 17–20%.
Expert commentary referencing the StZ/SWR poll and Infratest dimap data suggests the Landtag could expand to 180–220 seats, illustrating how distribution can affect apparent majorities.
SWP reports a tightening race with CDU still leading; current polling indicates CDU ahead of Greens in late Feb 2026, implying CDU could win the most seats if the lead persists.

The 2026 election is scheduled for March 8, 2026, with polls summarized as CDU in the high-20s to low-30s and Greens in the low-20s to mid-20s range small margins, suggesting CDU could win the most seats but margins remain close.

causal-factors.name: CDU polling lead in late February 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Polls from 25–26 February 2026 show CDU ahead of Greens by roughly 1–3 percentage points (e.g., 28% vs 27% and 27% vs 25%), with provisional seat projections giving CDU a small lead, which raises the probability of CDU winning the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Greens' historical strength and recent largest-party status
causal-factors.rationale: The Greens have been the largest party in 2016 and 2021, establishing a baseline that makes CDU winning the most seats less certain despite current poll leads.

causal-factors.name: Impact of the new Zweitstimme-based 154-seat system
causal-factors.rationale: The larger chamber and Zweitstimme dynamics can magnify vote concentration, potentially helping CDU to secure more seats relative to Greens in near-term projections.

causal-factors.name: AfD's sizable and volatile vote share
causal-factors.rationale: Polls show AfD around 18–21%; if AfD siphons more Green than CDU support, CDU's chances of remaining the largest party increase.

causal-factors.name: Turnout volatility and late campaign dynamics
causal-factors.rationale: Uncertain turnout, especially among Greens' core voters, could erase CDU's current margin and reduce its lead in seat tallies.

causal-factors.name: Narrow seat margin and sensitivity to small swings
causal-factors.rationale: Seat projections show a tight race (e.g., CDU 37 vs Greens 35; or 35 vs 32) meaning small shifts in votes in the final days could flip who has the most seats.

causal-factors.name: CDU polling lead and seat projections (late Feb 2026)
causal-factors.rationale: Several late-February 2026 polls place CDU ahead of Greens (roughly 27–29% vs 25–27%), with seat projections showing CDU ahead by a few seats in the 154-seat BW Landtag.

causal-factors.name: Greens' historical leadership in Baden-Württemberg (2016, 2021)
causal-factors.rationale: The Greens have led BW in 2016 and 2021, anchoring a baseline that reduces the likelihood of CDU being the largest party.

causal-factors.name: Electoral-system change and the 154-seat parliament (Zweitstimme-based)
causal-factors.rationale: The new electoral rules add uncertainty in translating polls into seats, with no clear directional bias yet.

causal-factors.name: Multi-party dynamics and potential late shifts involving AfD and other parties
causal-factors.rationale: Persistent AfD support and other party shares can sway seat allocations and affect who ends up with the most seats.

synthesis: Credible late polls show a CDU edge, but Greens’ recent dominance in BW history and the new electoral mechanics keep the outcome tight. The final probability is set at 0.43 with a modest 0.33–0.53 range to reflect remaining uncertainty.
